title: C482/1111/2021 of MOHAN LAL JOSHI Vs BRIJ MOHAN KALA

paras.text:
HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Criminal Misc. Application No.1111 of 2021
Mohan Lal Joshi ......Applicant
Versus

Shri Brij Mohan Kala ....Respondent
Present: Mr. Arvind Kumar Sharma, Advocate for the applicant.
Hon'ble Ravindra Maithani, J.(Oral)
 By means of instant petition, direction has been
sought for expeditious disposal of Criminal Case No.553 of
2020, Shri Mohan Lal Joshi vs. Shri Brij Mohan Kala, under
Section 138 Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881, pending in
the court of Judicial Magistrate, Rishikesh, District
Dehradun ("the Case").
2. In this matter on 26.08.2021, notices were issued
which have already been served on the private respondent.
3. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused
the record.
4. Learned counsel for the petitioner would submit
that the matter is not being heard expeditiously, therefore,
direction may be issued. This matter was heard on

2
05.03.2022, on that day, the Court passed the following
order;
"The petitioner seeks direction that the Criminal
Case No.553 of 2020, Shri Mohan Lal Joshi vs. Shri
Brij Mohan Kala, under Section 138 of the Negotiable
Instruments Act, 1881 be expedited.
The order sheet has been filed, which reveals
that on 14.09.2020, a complaint was filed and the
date was fixed for inquiry under Sections 202 of the
Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973. Thereafter, on
07.12.2020, 17.05.2021 and 05.08.2021, the matter
could not be taken due to COVID-19. There is no
other order sheet enclosed.
Let the petitioner give a statement what is the
status of the case today and file up-to-date order
sheets.
List once such order sheets are filed."
5. The complete order-sheet has now been filed by
the petitioner along with supplementary affidavit dated
20.03.2021. Petitioner is the complainant in this case. It is
the petitioner, who had filed the complaint. The
complainant was required to file his affidavit for inquiry
under Section 200 and 202 of the Code of Criminal
Procedure, 1973 ("the Code"), but the petitioner has not yet
filed such evidence. He did not adduce any evidence in the
inquiry under Sections 200 and 202 of the Code. The

3
complaint was filed on 04.09.2020. On that day, the matter
was adjourned for 07.12.2020. But it could not be taken up
on that date and on subsequent two more dates i.e. on
07.12.2020, 15.05.2021 and 05.08.2021.
6. On the next date i.e. on 01.11.2021, it is the
petitioner who filed his exemption application, but the
evidence for inquiry under Sections 200 and 202 of the
Code was not filed by the petitioner as required to be filed
by him by the order of the court dated 14.09.2020. It
appears that even nobody has seen as to what was going on
in the case. On 01.12.2021, the order-sheet records as
hereunder;
"Called out the case. The accused is absent.
Issue summons against the accused for 24.02.2022.
List on 24.02.2022 for appearance."
7. The cognizance order had not been passed till
01.12.2021, but the court ordered issuance of summons.
Nobody knows how it was done?
8. Learned counsel for the petitioner would agree
that the summons should not have been issued before
taking cognizance and passing an order for summoning.
9. Interestingly, on the next date i.e. 24.02.2022
again it is the petitioner who was absent. The delay, if any,
has been done by the petitioner. He has not filed an

4
evidence under Sections 200 and 202 of the Code.
Therefore, no directions are required.
10. Accordingly, the petition is liable to be dismissed.
11. The petition is dismissed.
12. However, the Court would like to invite the
attention of the learned Magistrate that on 01.12.2021,
summons were issued to the accused without any
cognizance order or any order for summoning. Summoning
of an accused is not a routine exercise. A person comes to
face the trial. It has its' consequence. Such errors would
touch upon the liberty of an individual, therefore, the courts
are expected to be little more cautious before processes are
issued.
13. Let a copy of this order be sent to the court
concerned through Registrar General of this Court.
